Macrons

Consonantal i

Kitchen, meals & drinks

pie noun

also apple pie, pumpkin pie

classical

Traupman 72

1crustum: short u (Traupman 70, 72 crūstum). As in crusta; Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked.

crustum1, crustī n.

noun, second declension

Examples

  • «Duo crusta faciēmus,» inquit pater, «alterum ex mālīs, alterum ex cucurbitā …»

    “We’ll make two pies,” said Dad, “one apple, the other pumpkinLibellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

  • Mēnsa deinde secunda in ferculō allāta est: crusta, alterum ex mālīs, alterum ex cucurbitā

    Then dessert was brought in on a tray: the pies, one apple, the other pumpkinLibellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

Other words

  • crustum ex mālīs — apple pie

    also used · modern · Traupman 70

  • crustum ex cucurbitā — pumpkin pie

    also used · our formation

    Descriptive, after Traupman’s pattern.

  • crustum cucurbitīnum — pumpkin pie

    also used · our formation

    The adjective cucurbitīnus is attested (Plin. NH XV 55, of a pear).

See also pie dish, vent, custard tart.

SourcesLewis & Short: crustum · Lewis & Short: cucurbitinus
